title: Understanding Model Bias
text: Model bias refers to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem by a simplified model. High bias can cause an algorithm to miss the relevant relations between features and target outputs.

title: Intercept in a Model
text: The intercept in a model represents the expected mean value of the dependent variable when all independent variables are zero. Removing it can sometimes lead to a better fit if the data naturally passes through the origin.

title: Effect of Removing Intercept
text: Removing the intercept forces the regression line to pass through the origin. This can increase bias if the true relationship does not pass through the origin.

hintAnswer: The model is forced to pass through the origin which may not fit the data well.
